source.title: Déjà Vu: an empirical evaluation of the memorization properties of ConvNets
source.authors: Alexandre Sablayrolles; Matthijs Douze; C. Schmid; H. Jégou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; some figure content is represented only by plots.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains ConvNets to memorize image membership and reports in/out accuracy and convergence under changes in image count and augmentation. This bears on fitting random labels, but uses a binary membership task rather than arbitrary random class labels.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly cites random-label experiments by Zhang et al. as prior work, which are not rows. Its own membership task assigns positive labels to selected images and negative labels to the rest; the resulting accuracy and convergence findings are rows. Figure 2 has no numeric values in the text, so its precise values are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Section 3 directly probes learning arbitrary binary labels by randomly selecting positive images and labeling the remaining images negative. This bears on V1 and the augmentation component of V5, although the task additionally requires rejecting unseen negatives. Membership-inference accuracy in Sections 4–5 does not test the claim. Convergence comparisons vary image count or augmentation, not true versus random labels or corruption fraction, so they do not test V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that ConvNets can explicitly memorize many images, with capacity and convergence affected by augmentation. Image-set membership remains detectable with full augmentation, whereas individual-image inference becomes less accurate. Intermediate layers retain membership information detectable above chance under limited augmentation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a binary in/out membership classifier with selected positive images and a large pool of negatives, rather than arbitrary random class labels on the original classification task. The paper cites Zhang et al.'s random-label finding but does not reproduce it.
record.method_sensitivity: Image count and data augmentation affect explicit memorization and convergence; the text says augmentation reduces memorization capacity and can increase convergence epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-16 and ResNet-101 converge in approximately the same number of epochs across positive-set sizes; augmentation increases convergence epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit image-membership learning has convergence costs that depend on augmentation and dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: Dataset detection and individual membership attacks recover information about training inclusion, including from intermediate layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained image classifiers retain detectable information about training-set membership.

record.problems: The explicit memorization plots do not provide numeric values in the supplied text. The binary in/out task differs from random-label classification and does not measure chance test error or true-label generalization. Large-architecture accuracy is not stated numerically in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 has separate curves for model, augmentation, and image count, but the flattened plot text does not preserve curve-to-value assignments and provides no exact numeric outcomes; summarized its qualitative text in R13-R18 rather than creating additional condition rows. Figures 1 and 2 have plot-only values; those settings are retained as figure-only rows where legible condition groups are supplied.

untested.parts: Chance test error on random class labels and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters relative to true-label classification. The membership task changes the output layer and samples fresh negatives.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and convergence as the corrupted-label fraction increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Weight decay and dropout effects on random-label fitting; generalization on true labels after removing explicit regularization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Arbitrary binary-label fitting is a direct capacity experiment relevant to this phenomenon. Its membership accuracy also requires negative rejection, so it is not interchangeable with ordinary random-label training error. Reduced capacity or slower convergence alone does not challenge V5, which does not assert that regularization has no effect. No support verdict for perfect fitting can be established from the unreadable plot endpoints or convergence statements.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test arbitrary random labels on the original classification task, report test error at chance, or compare the same model and hyperparameters on true labels.
Reports convergence in epochs for membership memorization, but does not compare training time against fitting true labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.

Tests whether augmentation changes explicit membership memorization capacity and convergence; does not test weight decay or dropout effects on arbitrary random labels, nor generalization on true labels after removing regularization.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained to distinguish selected positive images from negatives; text summarizes convergence across n.
rows.value: VGG-16 and ResNet-101 converge at approximately the same number of epochs, irrespective of n
rows.note: Authors note that epochs take 10× longer for n=100k than n=10k; the claim's small constant factor in training time is therefore not directly measured.
rows.check: Epoch counts across dataset sizes establish neither near-perfect fitting nor the random-versus-true-label time ratio in V2. An epoch takes ten times longer at 100k than at 10k positives.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Trained to distinguish selected positive images from negatives; text summarizes convergence across n.
rows.value: Data augmentation increases the number of epochs required to converge; for the ResNets, flip can require up to twice more epochs
rows.note: The text attributes increased convergence epochs to augmentation, not to a growing fraction of corrupted labels.
rows.check: Augmentation-dependent convergence time does not measure any version's specified effect. The statement concerns ResNets collectively, not uniquely ResNet-101.

rows.subject: ResNet-101
rows.operation_detail: Trained as a binary in/out classifier; text summarizes effect of data augmentation on memorization.
rows.measure: Ability to explicitly memorize a large amount of images
rows.value: Explicit memorization is possible, albeit more difficult with data augmentation
rows.note: This is a qualitative summary of the experiments; the paper does not claim all settings reach perfect accuracy.
rows.check: This is a pooled qualitative summary of Section 3.3, not a separate ResNet-101 measurement. It supplies no endpoint accuracy establishing perfect fitting; merge it into the relevant experimental rows.
